question.worked_solution:
To remove the radical $\sqrt{3}$ from the denominator, all we need to do is multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{3}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{8}}{\sqrt{3}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{8}}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{8}\cdot \sqrt{3}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{8}\cdot \sqrt{3}}{3} & \end{aligned}
$$

Next, we notice that $8$ has a perfect square factor $(4).$ Therefore, we can rewrite $\sqrt{8}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{8} & = \\ \sqrt{4\cdot 2} & = \\ \sqrt{4}\cdot \sqrt{2} & = \\ 2\sqrt{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify our original fraction as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{8}\cdot \sqrt{3}}{3} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{3}}{3} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{2\cdot 3}}{3} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
